endorsements.quote: Additionally, a cross-functional AI governance committee— including data scientists, clinicians, compliance officers, and ethics experts— should be established to review this data and make decisions throughou t the entire AI lifecycle.
Before any AI solution is pursued, governance frameworks must require a structured assessment of the underlying problem and a clear justification for why AI is the appropriate tool to solve it.
Healthcare enterprises should develop or enhance their data governance policies to include objective standards for data used in AI systems.
Healthcare organizations must independently validate the model’s performance on their own data to ensure that vendor-reported results hold true in their specific clinical or operational context.

Enterprises can strengthen their governance frameworks by requiring comprehensive documentation of AI model development, including data lineage, feature selection, validation methods, and bias mitigation strategies.
Enterprises should revise their governance frameworks to include continuous monitoring and postdeployment auditing of AI systems.
Ongoing oversight over AI implementations must focus on the monitoring of predefined Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).

A key risk management strategy for generative AI applications is redteaming, which involves testing the AI model under adversarial conditions to uncover potential vulnerabilities, biased outputs, or inaccuracies across diverse demographic groups.
In parallel, ongoing ethical review processes are essential for ensuring that generative AI applications align with healthcare values and patientcentered care.

AI governance committees should play a central role in reviewing and monitoring AI implementations, ensuring that AI systems meet enterprise standards for safety, efficacy, and ethical considerations.
This could involve establishing AI usage protocols that prevent over-reliance on AI recommendations, ensuring that human oversight r emains a key component of every operational work flow.

Finally, it is common to expect the enterprise audit team to develop a new department or contract externally specialized resources to periodically conduct manual audits of the AI model performance in production.

unlisted_practices: Consolidate enterprise AI compliance reporting into a centralized system that gathers all relevant data and incident reports in one place with clear accountability.
Incorporate safeguards to validate the integrity and provenance of all AI inputs, including AI-generated outputs fed back into systems, to prevent data poisoning.
Update training data to improve representation and adjust algorithm design to enhance fair performance when risks are identified.
